advice: Propose `libxsmm-transpose-direct-panel-consumption` as one end-to-end layout experiment. For each supported size, keep the existing full-call transpose as the control, then compare a changed fallback that packs A directly into the exact layout consumed by the FP32 outer-product kernel, removing the separate `at` buffer and transpose pass. Keep all packing and allocation inside `gemm`; preserve the n=512 panel32 dispatch unchanged. Measure transpose/packing, consumption, and total timed `gemm` cost for every supported `n`, with correctness over the existing 48 cases and tolerance 0.002. The supplied evidence gives no measurements for this experiment, so it is a hypothesis only. If direct packing cannot feed the existing consumer without changing arithmetic order or ABI, abstain rather than substitute a different kernel.
risks: The proposed direct layout and consumer integration are not specified by the supplied source, so implementation feasibility and any speed effect are unverified. Packing may cost as much as the transpose, require a larger allocation, or worsen consumer access. The n=512 path does not currently execute `sme_transpose`, so its frozen timing cannot measure fallback changes. Do not combine its result with fallback-size results or attribute a joint outcome to transpose alone. Preserve the existing fallback if allocation fails; include all allocation, packing, and consumption in timed calls.
